themes_detail.label: Street noise explosion
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints from streets and sidewalks spiked to 51 THIS WEEK—a 416% jump from the 9.9 weekly average—suggesting a sudden, acute disruption (construction, events, or illicit activity) requiring immediate investigation into what triggered the spike.
evidence: 51 street/sidewalk noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 9.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.23, severity: high)
416% spike represents most acute noise surge in 8-week period
Concurrent street condition spike (40 complaints this week vs. 12.4 avg) suggests shared underlying cause
reporting_angles: What construction or street activity started this week? Interview 311 complaint filers and locals.
Is this tied to a specific venue, street closure, or event? Cross-reference with DOE/DOT permits and event schedules.

themes_detail.label: Graffiti surge in Belmont
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints exploded to 16 LAST WEEK—a 753% jump from the 1.9 weekly average (z-score: 8.74, the highest statistical anomaly)—indicating either organized tagging or a breakdown in rapid-response removal.
evidence: 16 graffiti complaints last week vs. 1.9 weekly average (z-score: 8.74, highest severity spike in district)
753% increase—most extreme statistical outlier in all complaint categories
Spike concentrated in single week, suggests acute event or organized activity
reporting_angles: Did a crew target specific neighborhoods or landmarks? Survey affected block faces and interview property owners.
Is NYPD or Parks Dept. tracking organized tagging? Request enforcement and cleanup data.

themes_detail.label: Street infrastructure deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints jumped to 40 THIS WEEK—a 223% spike from the 12.4 weekly average—paired with dangling street signs (700% spike 3 weeks ago), signaling infrastructure decay across the district that poses safety and quality-of-life risks.
evidence: 40 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 12.4 weekly average (z-score: 4.57)
Dangling street sign complaints at 3 (3 weeks ago) vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% spike, z-score: 5.42)
Sustained infrastructure degradation signal: concurrent obstruction spike (300% this week)
reporting_angles: Walk major thoroughfares (East Tremont Ave, Third Ave, Southern Blvd) and document potholes, broken signs, sidewalk conditions. Get quotes from residents about commute and safety impact.
Does DOT have a maintenance backlog in Belmont/East Tremont? FOIL street repair requests and asset condition reports.

themes_detail.label: Encampment emergence
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints spiked to 5 LAST WEEK—a 471% jump from the 0.9 weekly average—indicating a sudden increase in unsheltered populations or visible street homelessness that may signal affordability crisis or service gaps.
evidence: 5 encampment complaints last week vs. 0.9 weekly average (z-score: 3.54)
471% spike in single week—rare complaint category now statistically significant
Community board budget history shows senior center and social services gaps (repeated requests for DFTA and DOE social programming)
reporting_angles: Where are encampments concentrated? Map complaints and conduct ground interviews with unhoused individuals about shelter capacity, access barriers.
Are local social service providers and nonprofits seeing increased demand? Interview them on capacity and funding needs.

themes_detail.label: Plumbing and construction surge
themes_detail.summary: General construction/plumbing complaints jumped to 11 LAST WEEK—a 238% spike from the 3.2 weekly average (z-score: 6.46)—suggesting either unpermitted work, water main issues, or increased development activity that may lack proper oversight.
evidence: 11 general construction/plumbing complaints last week vs. 3.2 weekly average (z-score: 6.46)
238% spike in single week; concurrent with 364 DOB permits filed over 90 days (134 new buildings, 194 alterations)
Belmont/East Tremont has active ULURP applications (Sojourner Truth-Mapes, 4506 Park Ave rezoning) suggesting development pipeline pressure
reporting_angles: Are unpermitted or improperly permitted projects driving complaints? Cross-reference 311 addresses against DOB permits and violation data.
Is the rezoning activity (ULURP applications) creating construction externalities? Interview contractors and community board on coordination.
